title: Sparse dictionary Mirror function representation
hypothesis: A paid shared functional atom dictionary plus sparse per-function addresses will reconstruct sparse-combination functions with fewer serialized bytes than independent dense functions while matching dense/signed coefficient controls at fixed distortion.
physical_object: one shared overcomplete dictionary of 64 atoms in 32D function space
mirror_coordinate: per-function sparse atom indices and signed scalar coefficients
logical_multiplicity: 128 reconstructed function vectors from a shared atom bank
controls: shared dictionary with dense FP16 coefficients
shared dictionary with signed 1-bit support coefficients
sparse dictionary Mirror codes with FP16 coefficients

task.type: synthetic 32D function vectors generated from 4-sparse shared atom combinations
metrics: support recovery and active atom count

development.allowed: select sparse threshold from registered top-k in {2,4,8,16}; shared dictionary learned only from development targets; no fresh-dependent fitting

paid_objects: per-function sparse indices and coefficient values

success_gate: At fixed top-4, every fresh world NRMSE <=0.05 and sparse payload <=50% independent dense bytes; report support recovery and compare dense/signed shared coefficient controls.
failure_gate: Sparse code misses quality/byte gate or dense/signed coefficient control matches quality at fewer bytes; report whether dictionary amortization is the limiting factor.
boundaries: Synthetic 4-sparse vector combinations only; not a trained network or language model.
Dictionary, indices, coefficients and all metadata charged.
Logical combination count is not capacity; only held-out reconstruction quality counts.
